name: Claudia A. Nasraty
headline: I Turn Moving Parts Into Forward Motion
tagline:
I build the structure, systems, and support that fast-moving teams need when their operations have not caught up with their pace. When that gap exists, priorities blur, follow-through breaks down, and leaders get pulled away from strategy. I step in to bring order, take ownership of what needs attention, and move the work forward.
When challenges surface, I do not wait to be asked. I take ownership, find a path forward, and see it through.
summary:
The way I work today took shape even before I had the language for it.

Early in my career, I joined Roshan, the leading telecommunications company in Kabul, Afghanistan at the time. The team was genuinely international, with colleagues from across the world working alongside local Afghan employees in a city where life outside the office was unpredictable in ways most workplaces are not. Getting things done there meant earning trust first. Trust was not given. It had to be built through how you showed up every single day. I learned what it really means to be reliable when the conditions are challenging. That has shaped how I show up in every environment since.

The relationships I have built throughout my career have lasted longer than the jobs themselves. Leaders I have worked alongside have brought me into their next companies. They had seen my work up close and trusted my abilities and judgment. That is probably what I’m most proud of.

What energizes me as a professional is improving how things work and making systems feel smoother, clearer, and more supportive for the people using them. I pay close attention to what is missing, what feels unclear, and where things may start to break down.

To me strong operations is what makes great work possible. It is not about adding process for the sake of it, but the kind of clarity, structure, and follow-through that removes the obstacles so people can focus on the work itself. 

I care just as much about the people side of the work as the operational structure. The best environments I have been part of are the ones where people communicate openly, support each other, and make it genuinely easier to move forward together. That is what I am always working toward, whether or not it is in my job description.

I use AI tools in my own workflow and guide the team by sharing what actually works in practice. I am less interested in the trend and more focused on whether it actually improves the work.

experience.title: Head of Business Operations
experience.description: I came in as employee #1, before there were any systems to inherit. I built the company's entire operational backbone from scratch: AR/AP, project costing, SOW and vendor trackers, SOPs, and the workflows the whole team runs on day to day. I manage end-to-end project operations across 3 to 5 concurrent qualitative research engagements, keeping co-founders, clients, and vendors aligned across a network of 28 vendors and 10 subcontractors. When the pipeline stalled, I built the company's first growth framework and stood up a HubSpot CRM with pipeline stages and structured follow-up workflows. I also designed a Research PM AI agent using Claude that is projected to save 4 to 8 hours per active recruiting project, and drove WBENC and Microsoft SSPA certifications to completion through multiple re-certification cycles.
experience.clients: Clients: Dell, Microsoft, Apple, AMD, LinkedIn, Instacart, Act Blue, Oxfam

experience.title: Associate Director of Operations
experience.description: Former Greenberg leaders brought me back to support the B2B Tech business unit through a messy post-acquisition transition, working with three co-leaders and eighteen team members. I brought structure to a team navigating real uncertainty: redesigned leadership meetings, wrote a team handbook from scratch, shaped the Workday rollout around how people actually worked, and launched a crowdsourced team development program with a three-phase curriculum. The role was eliminated in a company-wide restructure, but the structure I built outlasted my seat.

experience.title: Team Manager, Client Program Manager
experience.description: I came back to Greenberg as a senior leader, this time managing a team of three direct and one indirect report while running a full client load. I negotiated vendor rates down 20 to 25 percent and turned those relationships into vendor-funded research, a joint webinar, and speaking engagements. I also built the workflow processes, written playbooks, and onboarding documentation that standardized how every new CPM on the team got trained, and wrote the compliance documentation that carried us through a US Bank audit.

experience.title: Client Program Manager
experience.description: I managed five to seven concurrent global qualitative and quantitative research projects for Fortune 100 and 500 clients, with budgets running from $80K to $800K. On our first Wells Fargo engagement, a recruiting breakdown had quietly eroded client confidence. I introduced a call-logging process, traced the root cause to the client side, delivered the project on time, and turned a shaky start into a repeat relationship.

I built the billing, retainer tracking, and vendor payment systems across 20 to 30 media partners and contractors, and coordinated vendor logistics for client events ranging from 1,000 to 8,000 attendees. It was my first employee #1 moment, and it taught me how much I love being the person who turns a startup's blank page into something that actually runs.

experience.title: Account Coordinator

experience.title: Sr. Marketing Communications Specialist
experience.description: This is where it all started, and it shaped everything that came after. Roshan served over three million subscribers across 230 cities, and the environment — international, fast-moving, deeply multicultural — was unlike anything I had known. It taught me early that getting work done is never just about tasks and timelines. It is about listening first, earning trust, and understanding how people actually work together. When the moment called for it, I stepped up to lead a $700K youth segment campaign alongside the CMO, managing global agency partners including Grey Group and JWT, aligning five departments, and delivering a 40 percent increase in monthly acquisition and a record 230,000 activations.
